items.title: This remarkable mod transforms the most frightening horror game of the decade into Mirror's Edge
items.summary: Have faith in Bunker's Edge.
items.body: Amnesia: The Bunker is without a doubt the most frightening horror game I've played this decade. Its terrifying tale of being chased through a crumbling French bunker by a monster has the darkest, thickest, most unnerving atmosphere of any horror game I've played since Alien: Isolation . It's so intense that it's hard to imagine anyone making something light and airy out of its subterranean warrens, and it's downright inconceivable that someone might, say, turn Amnesia: The Bunker into Mirror's Edge. And yet, that's exactly what modder TiMan has done. Created for Frictional Games' 2026 modding jam —which ran with the theme of 'What is reality?'— Bunker's Edge sees the base game's protagonist Henri transported through a portal from the trenches of war-ravaged France to the pristine skyline of EA's free-running classic. The change of scenery alone is remarkable. The Bunker's HPL engine is purpose built to deliver darkness, shadows and murk, so seeing it handle such a bright and colourful environment is mightily impressive. items.body: حكم سابق يعلق على اللقطة الجدلية كشف الخبير التحكيمي برونو بايكساو رأيه في ركلة الجزاء التي حصل عليها ريال مدريد ضد رايو فاليكانو خلال مباراة الفريقين بالدوري الإسباني. وعاد ريال مدريد إلى سكة الانتصارات بفوز كبير قوامه 4-1 في المباراة التي أقيمت مساء أمس السبت على ملعب "سانتياجو برنابيو" ضمن الجولة الخامسة من الليجا. وعند الدقيقة 13، انطلق ألفارو كاريراس، ظهير ريال مدريد، من الجبهة اليسرى، وتوغل داخل منطقة الجزاء، قبل أن يتدخل فلوريان ليجويني، مدافع الفريق الضيف. واحتسب الحكم الإسباني فيكتور فيردورا ركلة جزاء للفريق الملكي، سجل منها كيليان مبابي هدف التقدم. واعترض لاعبو رايو فاليكانو على قرار الحكم، وطالبوه بالعودة إلى زميله في غرفة تقنية الفيديو المساعد، باعتبار أن المدافع لم يدهس قدم كاريراس بالصورة التي تستدعي احتساب ركلة جزاء. لكن الحكم البرتغالي السابق برونو بايكساو قال في تصريحات خاصة لكووورة إن "قرار الحكم سليم". وأوضح "لعب كاريراس الكرة أولًا، بينما ارتكب المدافع مخالفة واضحة ضده. لذلك كان قرار الحكم صحيحًا". ومن المقرر أن تكشف لجنة الحكام الإسبانية رأيها في هذه الحالة الجدلية بعد نهاية مباريات الجولة الخامسة من الليجا، عبر برنامجها الأسبوعي "وقت المراجعة". اقرأ أيضًا: خاص لكووورة.. خبير تحكيمي يسخر من قرار ركلة مبابي: لا نلعب كرة سلة! من هو برونو بايكساو؟ ويعد برونو بايك…

items.body: حارس الميرينجي السابق سلط الضوء على سلبيات الخط الأمامي انتقد سانتي كانيزاريس، حارس ريال مدريد السابق، ما اعتبره ضعف انخراط من مهاجمي الفريق الملكي في المهام الدفاعية، وذلك بعد الفوز أمس السبت على رايو فاليكانو (4-1) في ملعب سانتياجو برنابيو، ضمن منافسات الجولة الخامسة من الليجا. ولم يتردد كانيزاريس في انتقاد أداء الميرينجي خلال تحليله للمباراة عبر إذاعة "كوبي" ، قائلاً: "مدريد يملك فضيلة، أفضل فضيلة يمكن أن يملكها فريق، وهي الفاعلية، لا شك في ذلك"، محذّراً من أن "الفريق إذا أراد أن يكون الأفضل في أوروبا، عليه أن يجيد أكثر من جانب". اقرأ أيضًا برشلونة أم ريال مدريد.. صحيفة إسبانية تكشف عن حلم الزابيري نجم ألمانيا الصاعد يقطع أولى خطواته مع برشلونة وتطرق كانيزاريس بشكل خاص إلى ضعف انخراط مهاجمي ريال مدريد في الدفاع، بقوله: "حين لا يملكون الكرة، ما يفعله المهاجمون أمر مروّع. يعدي بعضهم بعضاً، واحد ينظر إلى الآخر، والآخر ينظر إلى الآخر، ويقول: آه، أنا، إذا هذا لا يتحرك، أنا أيضاً لا أتحرك". وتابع: "الفريق ينقسم، ويضطر لاعبو الوسط إلى التراجع والالتصاق بالدفاع، وأي فريق يصنع فرصاً على ريال مدريد". وشدد حارس الميرينجي السابق على أن هذا الأمر يمثل مشكلة تنافسية للفريق، موضحاً: "هذا غير تنافسي، ويجب حلّه. إذا لم تفعل ذلك طوال السنة، فاليوم الذي يحين فيه فعله قد لا تفعله بشكل جيد تماماً".…

After two years in development and more column inches of enthusiastic preview copy than is healthy, Revolution Software and Dave Gibbons' Beneath A Steel Sky, finally, arrives. And it couldn't be further removed from the Hull-based company's 1992 debut. After the magic and mythology of Lure Of The Temptress comes an oppressive, futuristic techno-thriller that borrows heavily from the pioneering sci-fi works of Philip K Dick and William Gibson. items.title: Why is Blizzard still announcing games years ahead of release? 'We want to convey confidence in some of our biggest bets coming forward'
items.summary: Maybe it's the fact it sounds like a year from the opening crawl of a sci-fi movie, but 2030 sure feels a long way off.
items.body: Reactions to the StarCraft trailer shown at BlizzCon this year seem pretty universal. Initial excitement, immediately deflated when the words "STARCRAFT RETURNS 2030" appeared at the end. (The fact it's going to be an "open world shooter" didn't help.) The surprise announcement of Diablo 5 coming in 2029 seems odd too. There were 11 years between Diablo 3 and Diablo 4, but the gap between that and Diablo 5 will only be six. Announcing videogames more than a couple of years ahead of release feels like a relic of the past. Everyone assumes games will get delayed anyway, and viewers are adding "at the earliest" as a footnote. Saying something is just around the corner earns goodwill, while saying it's three or four years away tells us to gear up for a hype cycle we'll be tired of before the actual game materializes—if it ever does. Blizzard president Johanna Faries spoke to Bloomberg ahead of BlizzCon. "We want to convey confidence in some of our biggest bets coming forward," she said on this topic. items.summary: Blizzard has offered up a surprising amount of detail about the action RPG sequel, which won't be out until 2029.
items.body: Diablo 5 is shaping up to be very different from Diablo 4. The sequel is set a hundred years after Diablo 4 in the aftermath of Diablo (the demon)'s apocalyptic destruction of Sanctuary, and it's going to bring fundamental changes to combat, classes, and loot. Several Diablo 5 developers took the stage today at BlizzCon 2026 to talk about their vision for the game, noting that everything is still a work-in-progress and subject to change between now and the spring 2029 release window. A lot of Diablo 5's biggest changes feel like a response to both player reception of Diablo 4—specifically what it lacked compared to previous games and competitors, like Path of Exile—and the much darker setting, which Blizzard is "doubling down" on. The campaign begins several years after a golden age for Sanctuary, right as it falls into the hands of the big bad Diablo. Like Mephisto in Diablo 4, Diablo will be a full character as opposed to just a boss you fight at the end. Much of the story will involve restoring the western continent and Westmarch, the most iconic location in the series, from its ravaged state. items.summary: The Diablo team is "all focused on seasons and getting to Diablo 5," support for Diablo 4 will continue "for a very long time," says Blizzard.
items.body: Diablo is returning: At BlizzCon today, Blizzard announced that Diablo 5 will be set a century after Diablo 4 in a Sanctuary that has succumbed to the Lord of Terror, Diablo himself. That's not until 2029, though. In the meantime, Blizzard will continue the story of Diablo 4 with seasons, but no more expansions are currently planned for the game. "We're all focused on [Diablo 4] seasons and getting to Diablo 5," said Diablo game director Brent Gibson in an interview with PC Gamer at BlizzCon. "We feel like we told the Story of Hatred. We had a great conclusion with Lord of Hatred with what we have with Mephisto, and we are moving towards telling the Story of Terror." Even if no more expansions are currently planned, the Diablo 4 story isn't over. Given the premise of Diablo 5, Blizzard now has to bring about the apocalypse, and it sounds like we'll see how that plays out in the upcoming seasons. Nothing's set in stone, though. WoW: Forever will explore new parts of Azeroth, telling stories that weren't told during the MMO's original progression. Now it's looking to expand its reach even further by giving Roblox creators the ability to release their work as standalone games. Part of Roblox's immense popularity can be attributed to the fact that it's not just a game, it's a platform where people can create and share their own games, and earn money on them. Which is weird, given that Kojima's a bit of an auteur—his games are weird and ambitious in scope, but they're often viewed fondly, and the man made Metal Gear Solid, for crying out loud. Physint was meant to be a return to "tactical espionage action", a prodigal return to what he's known for—it seems wild to drop it, something Xbox decided to capitalise on, snapping up the project instantly . It's since broken, in a Bloomberg report , that Sony might've simply ran out of patience. items.body: If you've been keeping up with the headlines, then you know gaming hasn't been Nvidia's main priority for some time now. Given that its data centre segment made $89 billion in Q2 of 2026 —an eye-watering 93% of the company's total revenue that quarter—it's not super surprising that Nvidia is all-in on AI. What may be surprising though is that, even after this shift in focus, Nvidia is still king when it comes to consumer GPUs. That's according to the latest report from John Peddie Research ; even though Nvidia's market share did decrease by 0.01% last quarter, the company is still holding on to a 90% share of the graphics 'Add-in Board' (AIB) market. items.body: So you've just been shot in Battlefield and now you're lying in a mass of other players' bodies, all of you hammering the 'REVIVE MEEE' request button as medics buzz about, helping everyone but you. If only there was a way to show them how important you are, that your life is clearly worth more than Skidz69 over there. How about money ? Wardogs is a Battlefield-style shooter where you can pay for just about anything, from a fancy loadout, to a literal taxi ride to the conflict zone. Earning cash for doing what you want is a really smart way of incentivising the whole battlefield role fantasy, whether you're building fortifications and sure-ing up your faction's forward operating base, or dragging downed players out of the fire and rezzing them. Though factions can win and lose, Wardog's only true language of success is profitability , more cash to buy fancier hardware, which you use to earn more cash. It's a wonderfully fitting and nihilistic approach to all-out warfare—each life is an investment in what you're going to do that run. Whether it pays off is where the true play comes in.
